Every run produces three artifacts:

- **output.xml** — the machine-readable source of truth.
- **log.html** — the detailed log: every test, keyword, argument, and message.
- **report.html** — the high-level summary: pass/fail counts and timings.

The console gives you the quick verdict per test; the log tells you *why*. When
a test fails, the log is where you look first. Use `--outputdir` to keep these
files in one place instead of your project root.

```diagram
pipeline "A run and its artifacts"
robot #robot -- uv run robot
arrow writes
output.xml #doc -- machine-readable source of truth
arrow open
report.html #doc -- summary: pass/fail counts
log.html #doc -- detail: every keyword and message
note "log.html and report.html are both views of output.xml"
```

## Task 1 — Run the suite into an output directory

Run your suite and send the artifacts to `results/`:

```bash
uv run robot --outputdir results checks
```

You'll see the run report each test and tally the result:

```terminal
$ uv run robot --outputdir results checks
==============================================================================
Checks.First Suite
==============================================================================
Greeting Reads Clean                                                  | PASS |
------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Checks.First Suite                                                    | PASS |
==============================================================================
1 test, 1 passed, 0 failed
==============================================================================
```

Robot Framework writes `results/output.xml`, `results/log.html`, and
`results/report.html`.

**Check:** the run produced `results/log.html` and `results/report.html`.

## Task 2 — Read log.html and report.html

Open `results/report.html` for the summary, then `results/log.html` and expand
the test to see each keyword and its message. This is the habit that makes
failures quick to diagnose later.

**Check:** nothing to run — continue once you have opened both files.
